The command snmpwalk -v 1 192.222.206.3 -c public performs an SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) query using version 1 of the protocol to the device at IP address 192.222.206.3. It uses the community string public (often the default read-only community string) to recursively retrieve and display all SNMP data available from the target device, providing details about its configuration, interfaces, and other system information.

The command snmpwalk -c public 192.222.206.3 -v1 -On | grep '.1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0' is used to query an SNMP-enabled device (with IP address 192.222.206.3) using the SNMP community string public and SNMP version 1. The command retrieves and filters information to find the system name, which is represented by the OID .1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0

The command snmpset -v 1 -c public 192.222.206.3 ‘.1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0’ s sets the value of the SNMP OID (Object Identifier) .1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0, which typically represents the system's hostname, to a new value (though the new value isn't specified in the command). It uses SNMP version 1 (-v 1) with the community string "public" (-c public) to make changes on the device with IP address 192.222.206.3.

The command snmpwalk -c public 192.222.206.3 -v1 -On | grep ‘.1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0’ performs an SNMP walk using the community string "public" on the device with IP 192.222.206.3, using SNMP version 1, and displays OID values in numeric form. methodology.name: Enumerating  Ports
methodology.intro: When it comes to network VAPT there will be services that are very commonly seen, for example, HTTP, SSH, FTP, and more. But then there are services that are not widely used, these services are deployed on the network for a specific usage. These services can give us an idea of the network architecture and use case.

rows.method:
Researching the port: https://www.speedguide.net/ports.php - This website will give us info on what services, exploits and malware use what ports
We can enumerate using the port number and fetch info like protocol, services and service details.
https://whatportis.com/ports - This website give us an idea on which ports are commonly used and which may have security threats to them and can be exploited.
https://tcp-udp-ports.com/ - Port details based on OS , Services and information on each port

Researching the service: Once the service is confirmed by Nmap scan and speedguide.net. we can do a quick Google search "Enumerating <service-name>"
If we have results from websites like
https://book.hacktricks.xyz/ - this website provides a guide on pen-testing this service
Any github repo - can give us an understanding of the service, it can also be some service enumerating script.
Rapid7 - msf modules that can be used against this service.
nmap - NSE script against this service
Other - we can find other interesting websites and articles on the service which can give us an understanding on the service.

Understanding the environment: While researching the service we also get an idea of what kind of environment uses this service. Based on the environment this service can be used for information gathering, exploitation, or any post-exploitation attacks.
Refer to all other technical blogs in the search results to get an idea on the service and the environment. We can also do a Google search combining the service and the port "<service> port" and we can have multiple articles on the usage of that service. This will also give us an idea on which devices these services are used.

CTFs Related to Service: We can search "<service> CTF" and we will find results with some blogs and posts for CTFs in which this service was used or seen. This gives us an idea on how to approach this service and what are few attack vectors.
rows.remarks:
This is a research phase. The idea here is to understand the service, and maybe find some interesting scripts that can be used in the process of understanding the service.
We are not worried about exploitation at this phase we want to understand the service and its use case.
